translation:
  text: '“Those who handed in rods that were half green and half dry are people entangled in business
    affairs who do not keep close to the holy ones. For this reason, half of them is alive and half is
    dead.”[a]


    2. “Many heard my commandments and repented. Those who repented have their dwelling in the tower.
    But some turned away completely. These have no repentance: because of their business affairs, they
    blasphemed and denied the Lord. So they lost their life through the wickedness they committed.”[b]


    3. “Many among them wavered. These still have an opportunity to repent if they repent quickly, and
    their dwelling will be in the tower. If they repent more slowly, they will dwell in the walls. But
    if they do not repent, they too have lost their life.”


    4. “Those who handed in rods that were two-thirds green and one-third dry are people who denied in
    various ways.”[c]


    5. “Many among them repented and went to dwell in the tower. But many turned away from God completely;
    they lost their life completely. Some among them wavered and caused divisions. These still have an
    opportunity to repent if they repent quickly and do not persist in their pleasures. But if they persist
    in their deeds, they too bring death upon themselves.”[d]'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: 'Pragmateiai means business or practical affairs. “Holy ones” renders hagioi as the community’s
      people; alternative: “saints.” The half-alive/half-dead image remains distinct from complete death.
      Michigan loses about nine lines over most of this opening, Bonner printed p. 108, so cannot certify
      the whole paragraph.'
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The working text says these people have no repentance; Michigan has “no longer,” Bonner printed
      p. 108. Alternative: “These no longer have repentance.” The statement concerns the group that turned
      away completely, blasphemed and denied the Lord; the following paragraph separately gives the wavering
      group a conditional opportunity.'
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'Two-thirds green and one-third dry is the 1891 edition’s version-supported correction. Athos
      reverses the colors: “Those who handed in rods that were two-thirds dry and one-third green are
      people who denied in various ways.” Michigan has a gap of about nine lines here, Bonner printed
      p. 109, and cannot decide the proportions. The draft provisionally retains the working correction,
      recording the Athos alternative rather than claiming unanimous Greek evidence. The object of denied
      is implicit in Greek; no new explicit object is inserted.'
  - marker: d
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The 1891 text has an opportunity to repent; Michigan explicitly has “still,” Bonner printed
      p. 109. Alternative: “These still have an opportunity to repent.” This idiomatic still is included
      in the English as continuing opportunity, not unconditional salvation. “Completely” preserves the
      repeated eis telos without selecting an unstated precise duration; alternative sense: “to the end.”
      The quick-repentance and no-continuing-pleasures conditions, and the warning about persistent deeds,
      remain explicit.'
lexical_decisions:
- source_word: μετάνοια / διψυχεῖν
  chosen: repentance / waver
  alternatives:
  - turning back / be double-minded
  rationale: Retain distinct groups, response conditions and warnings. An opportunity to repent is not
    the same as actual repentance or achieved salvation.
- source_word: πραγματεῖαι / εἰς τέλος
  chosen: business affairs / completely
  alternatives:
  - practical affairs / to the end
  rationale: Preserve the practical entanglement and the repeated finality language without imposing a
    precise duration not stated by the Greek.
